ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Bead Densification and Processing Coupled to Single-Molecule Array (DMF-Simoa) for Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - TNF-alpha Sample (solution of TNF-alpha antigen, 100 uL aliquot)
  - Simoa Capture Beads (anti-TNF-alpha antibody-coated superparamagnetic beads, 25 uL suspension containing 15000 functionalized beads)
  - Biotinylated Detection Antibody (anti-TNF-alpha detection antibody, 20 uL aliquot)
  - Wash Buffer (PBS containing 0.01% w/v Tetronic 90R4 surfactant)
  - Streptavidin-beta-Galactosidase (SbG) Reagent (enzyme label conjugate)
  - RGP Substrate (resorufin-beta-D-galactopyranoside fluorogenic substrate)

STEPS:
1. Off-chip pre-incubation: Mix the 100 uL TNF-alpha sample, 25 uL bead suspension (15000 beads), and 20 uL detection antibody together; incubate for 20 min off-chip on a shaker at 800 rpm to form antibody-antigen-bead sandwich immunocomplexes.
2. Stepwise sample loading onto DMF: Dispense the entire pre-incubated sample-bead mixture onto the sample reservoir electrode; sequentially load, split, and remove waste from ~9 uL segments over ~12 closed-loop, capacitance-monitored cycles to fully transfer the sample into the device while retaining beads on the densifying electrode (>98% bead retention).
3. Bead washing: Wash the densified beads with fresh wash buffer over multiple wash cycles (5 repeats) to remove unbound sample components.
4. SbG incubation: Deliver the streptavidin-beta-galactosidase reagent to the densified beads and incubate for 5 min at 25C to label captured immunocomplexes with enzyme.
5. Post-SbG washing: Wash the labeled beads again with fresh wash buffer over multiple wash cycles (5 repeats) to remove excess unbound SbG.
6. Substrate addition and detection: Deliver the RGP (resorufin-beta-D-galactopyranoside) substrate to the washed, labeled beads and incubate for 30 min at 25C to allow enzymatic conversion to fluorescent resorufin; the processed bead suspension is then collected and transferred to a microtiter plate/SR-X imager, where beads are loaded into femtoliter-sized microwells and imaged to determine the average number of enzyme labels per bead (digital single-molecule readout), then the analyzed droplet is discarded.

INTERPRETATION: Successful DMF-Simoa TNF-alpha quantification is confirmed by calibration curves of average enzyme labels per bead vs. TNF-alpha concentration obtained via the DMF-processed workflow that are comparable to those obtained via conventional manual microtiter-plate Simoa processing, with more than 98% bead retention during stepwise sample loading and no significant loss of assay sensitivity, supporting the feasibility of a miniaturized, automated DMF-Simoa platform for ultrasensitive biomarker detection.

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Macrophage memory emerges from coordinated transcription factor and chromatin dynamics
Source Link  : https://www.cell.com/cell-systems/pdfExtended/S2405-4712(25)00004-3
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2025.101171
Journal      : Cell Systems, 2025, Vol. 16, Article 101171
Platform     : Automated microfluidic live-cell imaging (PDMS multilayer, 64-chamber device) +
               off-chip ATAC-seq (Illumina NovaSeq SP) + off-chip RNA-seq (Illumina NextSeq550)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a multi-modal experimental pipeline for profiling innate immune memory
in primary bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) from RelA(mVenus/mVenus) (RelA^V/V) transgenic
mice. RelA is the canonical NF-kB transcription factor (TF); its endogenous mVenus tag enables
single-cell live imaging of nuclear translocation dynamics as a direct readout of inflammatory
signalling state.

The protocol is divided into five functional phases:
  1. BMDM differentiation and microfluidic device preparation
  2. Systematic sequential inflammatory ligand stimulation screen (80 conditions;
     two representative arms encoded: polyI:C -> TNF-a and CpG -> TNF-a)
  3. Live-cell NF-kB dynamics imaging and QC gating
  4. ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility profiling (single and sequential stimulus conditions)
  5. RNA-seq transcriptomic profiling and synergy/antagonism classification

A deep-learning multilayer perceptron (MLP) model integrating NF-kB dynamics features (48)
and chromatin accessibility + TF motif features (133) achieves 72.8% accuracy in predicting
memory-conditioned gene expression across four expression classes -- an improvement of >30%
over random assignment (38.7%). The work demonstrates that inflammatory memory is encoded at
two levels: reprogramming of the NF-kB signalling network (network memory) and remodelling of
the chromatin accessibility landscape (chromatin memory), and that both are required for full
predictive power.


MOUSE MODEL
-----------
Strain     : RelA(mVenus/mVenus) C57BL/6J (RelA^V/V); endogenous mVenus-RelA knock-in
Age        : 6-12 weeks (BMDMs); 6-8 weeks (peritoneal macrophage / endotoxemia experiments)
Sex        : Male and female
Housing    : Specific pathogen-free (University of Chicago; UCLA)
Ethics     : NIH Guide for Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; IACUC approval (U Chicago / UCLA)
Reference  : Adelaja et al., Immunity 2021 (original RelA^V/V line description)


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Type       : PDMS multilayer microfluidic device; 64 independent cell-culture chambers; 14 inputs
Control    : Electronically actuated pneumatic solenoid valves; custom MATLAB graphical interface
             or pre-written automation scripts
Tubing     : PEEK (VICI); input pressure 4 psi to minimise cell shearing during feeding
Microscope : Nikon Ti2 epifluorescence; 20x magnification
Camera     : Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash4.0 V2
Channels   : mVenus-RelA (508 nm excitation, 1 s exposure); Hoechst (395 nm, 50 ms exposure)
Interval   : 6-min imaging frames; total window 8-16 h per experiment
Environment: Life Imaging Services apparatus; 37 C / 5% CO2 / 98% humidity
Coating    : 0.2-0.4 mg/mL human fibronectin (R&D Systems 1918-FN) in PBS; overnight coat;
             flushed with complete media before cell loading
Master mold: Silicon wafer; previously published design (Son et al., Sci Signal 2021)

In vivo model (peritoneal macrophages):
  LPS dose : 12.5 mg/kg i.p. in PBS (sublethal endotoxemia)
  Timepoint: 4 h post-injection; peritoneal lavage (ice-cold PBS + 1% FBS + 2 mM EDTA)
  Isolation: Negative selection via Macrophage Isolation Kit (Miltenyi Biotec 130-110-434),
             MACS MS system
  Result   : TNF-a response significantly attenuated; LPS response completely abolished
             vs sham PBS-injected littermates (3 independent pairs)


CULTURE CONDITIONS
------------------
Complete macrophage culture media (RPMI-based):
  RPMI-1640 base
  10% heat-inactivated FBS (Omega)
  1% penicillin/streptomycin (Lonza/Corning)
  1% NEAA (Corning)
  1% HEPES (Gibco/Corning)
  1% sodium pyruvate (Corning)
  1% L-glutamine (Fisher/Corning)
  0.1% beta-mercaptoethanol (Gibco)
  Supplement: 20 ng/mL recombinant murine m-CSF (Peprotech 315-02-10UG)

Live-cell imaging media: phenol-red-free RPMI (Gibco) to minimise background fluorescence.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | BMDM Differentiation (Days 0-7)
  Source     : Femurs and tibias of 6-12 week old RelA^V/V mice
  Protocol   : Bone marrow cells cultured in complete media + 20 ng/mL m-CSF for 7-9 days
  Feed days  : Day 2, Day 4, Day 6 (fresh complete media + m-CSF added)
  Day 7 lift : Wash with PBS; lift adherent BMDMs with 10 mM EDTA (Fisher) in PBS (Gibco)
  Resuspension: 10^7 cells/mL in phenol-red-free RPMI for device loading
  BioScript  : Three sequential culture_D2/D4/D6 mix operations (2880m each = 48 h each);
               lift modelled as mix with PBS (1440m)

Step 2 | Microfluidic Device Preparation
  Coating    : 0.2-0.4 mg/mL fibronectin in PBS; fill chambers; overnight (480m in BioScript)
  Flush      : Complete media; 10 min (10m in BioScript)
  Mount      : Nikon Ti2; set to 37 C / 5% CO2 / 98% humidity before cell loading

Step 3 | Hoechst Staining and Cell Loading
  Stain      : 1 uM Hoechst 33342 in complete media; 5 min (5m); wash with complete media
  Load       : Cells loaded into device; adhere ~30 min before imaging starts
  Tracking   : >99% cell tracking accuracy over 8-h intervals (Video S3, paper supplemental)
  BioScript  : deviceWithCells_arm1 (Arm 1: polyI:C -> TNFa chambers)
               deviceWithCells_arm2 (Arm 2: CpG -> TNFa chambers; separate chamber set)
               NOTE: These are split variables (FIX #3) to prevent double-consumption in IR.

Step 4 | Sequential Ligand Stimulation Screen (80 conditions; 2 arms encoded)
  Design     : Ligand A (identity x dose x duration) -> Ligand B (TNF-a or LPS)
               6 ligands A x 3-4 doses x 2 durations (4h, 8h) x 2 Ligand B = 80 conditions
  Delivery   : Ligands diluted in complete media + m-CSF immediately before use;
               stored on ice; delivered via PEEK tubing at 4 psi
  Controls   : Positive: media -> 10 ng/mL TNFa; media -> 1 ng/mL LPS
               Negative: complete media only
  Replicates : > 300 individual cells per condition; >= 2 independent preparations

  Arm 1 (PRIMING): polyI:C -> TNF-a
    Ligand A : polyI:C (HMW, Invivogen tlrl-pic); 300 ng/mL in complete media + m-CSF
               Duration: 4 h (240 min) via channel perfusion
               Pathway : TLR3/TRIF -> NF-kB activation
               Effect  : Priming; normalised AUC > 1 (> naive Ligand B response)
    Ligand B : TNF-a (R&D Systems 410-MT-010/CF); 10 ng/mL; 4 h (240 min)
               NF-kB Nuc/Cyto ratio tracked at 6-min intervals throughout

  Arm 2 (TOLERANCE): CpG -> TNF-a
    Ligand A : CpG (ODN 1668, Invivogen tlrl-1668); 100 nM in complete media + m-CSF
               Duration: 4 h (240 min) via channel perfusion
               Pathway : TLR9/MyD88 -> NF-kB activation
               Effect  : Tolerance; normalised AUC < 1 (< naive Ligand B response)
    Ligand B : TNF-a; 10 ng/mL; 4 h (240 min)

  Other ligands in full screen (not encoded in .bs; same structural pattern):
    LPS (Invivogen tlrl-3pelps): 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 ng/mL; tolerising
    TNF-a (R&D 410-MT-010/CF) : 1, 3, 10, 30 ng/mL; tolerising (TNF self-tolerance only)
    PAM2CSK4 (Invivogen)       : 30, 100, 300 pg/mL; tolerising
    IL-1b (R&D 401-ML-010/CF)  : 3, 10, 30 ng/mL; largely indistinguishable from naive

Step 5 | NF-kB Dynamics Imaging and Analysis (Protocol 3)
  Module     : nfkbDynamicsDetection (BioScript); 240m (4h) detect window
  Readout    : RelA-mVenus nuclear/cytoplasmic (Nuc/Cyto) ratio per cell per frame
  Processing : MATLAB 2021a; custom code (GitHub: taylab/macrophage_memory)
               Flat field + dark frame correction
               Hoechst-based nuclear segmentation and multi-frame cell tracking
               Background subtraction from cell-free image regions
               Trace filtering: remove dead, divided, or artefact cells
  Metrics    :
    AUC          : Trapezoidal approximation over 240 min Ligand B window
    Early AUC    : First 120 min (20 frames)
    Late AUC     : Last 120 min (20 frames)
    Max amplitude: Index of max from loess-smoothed trace (3-frame window, min prominence 0.1);
                   Nuc/Cyto ratio at that index from unsmoothed trace
    Peak timing  : First frame at half-maximal amplitude
    Normalisation: AUC' (memory-conditioned) / AUC_0 (mean naive Ligand B AUC)
  Memory classification:
    Normalised AUC > 1 -> priming
    Normalised AUC < 1 -> tolerance
  Mutual information:
    Method : Jetka et al. 2019, PLOS Comp Biol (software package MIToolbox)
    Input  : Dynamic vector of 20 evenly-spaced timepoints over 4 h stimulus interval
    Range  : 0 bits (indistinguishable) to 1 bit (fully distinguishable)
    Finding: Up to 0.9 bits MI between polyI:C-primed vs naive TNF-a responses;
             dynamic trace MI >> single-feature (max amplitude) MI across all conditions

  QC gate (BB2/BB3):
    Pass (BB2): nfkbPrimingSignal > 0 -> dispose(stimulatedArmB)
    Fail (BB3): nfkbPrimingSignal <= 0 -> drain(stimulatedArmB)

Step 6 | ATAC-seq Chromatin Accessibility Profiling (Protocol 4)
  Replating  : 7.5e5 BMDMs/well in 6-well plate; overnight rest in complete media + m-CSF
  Stimulation: Single stimulus (polyI:C 1 ug/mL, CpG 100 nM, LPS 1 ng/mL, TNF-a 10 ng/mL);
               4 h each. Sequential conditions (polyI:C/CpG -> TNF-a/LPS; 4h + 4h).
               Representative encoded in .bs: polyI:C single stimulus (1 ug/mL, 240m)
  Cell lift  : Accutase (ThermoFisher) + gentle scraping; 5e4 cells per reaction
  Nuclei isolation:
    Lysis buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 / 3 mM MgCl2 / 10 mM NaCl / 0.1% IGEPAL CA-630
    Temperature : 4 C (cold lysis, on ice)
    Centrifugation: 10 min at 500 x g (BioScript: heat at 4c for 10m)
  Transposase reaction:
    Mix: 25 uL 2X TD Buffer + 2.5 uL TD Enzyme 1 (Illumina) + 22.5 uL nuclease-free water
    Conditions: 37 C, 30 min, 800 rpm shaking (BioScript: heat at 37c for 30m)
    Purification: MinElute PCR purification kit (Qiagen)
  PCR amplification:
    Primers  : Illumina Nextera sequencing primers
    Extension: 72 C initial (5 min); cycles: 98C/30s -> 63C/30s -> 72C/1min (~12 cycles)
    BioScript: heat at 72c for 30m (simplified PCR hold abstraction)
    Pool and sequence on Illumina NovaSeq SP, 50 bp paired-end
  Bioinformatics:
    Alignment        : bowtie2 v2.2.5 (mm10); MAPQ > 30; --very-sensitive --non-deterministic
    Deduplication    : Picard MarkDuplicates v2.18.29
    Peak calling     : MACS3 v3.0.0b1; FDR 0.01; -f BAMPE; -g mm; --nomodel
    Peak merging     : Iterative overlap peak merging (Corces et al. 2018, Science)
    Quantification   : featureCounts (R/Bioconductor)
    Differential acc.: edgeR + limma; vs media control
    Motif enrichment : monaLisa (R/Bioconductor) with JASPAR2022 database
    Peak annotation  : ChIPseeker (R/Bioconductor)
    Track visualisation: Rtracklayer (R/Bioconductor)
  Data deposited: GEO GSE261647

  Key chromatin findings:
    - polyI:C and CpG produce distinct chromatin accessibility patterns (Fig 5B)
    - Shared motifs: kB (RelA, NFKB1/2) and AP-1 (Fos, Jun) in all upregulated groups
    - polyI:C-specific: ISRE (Irf3, Irf8, Irf9) motifs co-occur with RelA peaks
    - CpG-specific: c/EBP (beta, gamma) motifs co-occur with RelA peaks
    - Sequential stimuli: chromatin landscape primarily encodes FIRST stimulus identity
      (Spearman r ~0.79 with first-stimulus-only vs ~0.37-0.44 with second-stimulus-only)

  QC gate (BB5/BB6):
    Pass (BB5): atacSignal > 0 -> dispose(atacLibrary)
    Fail (BB6): atacSignal <= 0 -> drain(atacLibrary)

Step 7 | RNA-seq Transcriptomic Profiling (Protocol 5)
  Replating  : 1.5e5 BMDMs/well in 24-well plate; overnight rest in complete media + m-CSF
  Conditions : polyI:C -> TNF-a; CpG -> TNF-a; polyI:C -> LPS; CpG -> LPS
               (4h Ligand A -> aspirate -> 4h Ligand B -> aspirate -> RLT lysis)
               Representative encoded in .bs: polyI:C -> TNF-a
  Replicates : Triplicate (n=3 per condition)
  Lysis      : RLT buffer (Qiagen) + 1% beta-mercaptoethanol
  RNA extraction: Dynabeads (Invitrogen)
  RT         : Maxima HMinus RT (Thermo Fisher); poly-dT oligo + TSO
               (5'-AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTGAATRGGG-3'); 55 C, 60 min
               BioScript: heat at 55c for 60m
  2nd strand : KAPA HiFi (Roche); primer: 5'-AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGT-3'; 1 cycle
  Purification: Ampure XP beads (Beckman Coulter)
  Library prep: Nextera XT (Illumina FC-131-1024); mean fragment size 400-600 bp
  Sequencing : NextSeq550 (Illumina), NextSeq 500/550 high output kit v2 (cat. 20024906)
  Bioinformatics:
    Alignment        : STAR (GRCm38/mm10 reference); default parameters
    Quantification   : featureCounts (R/Bioconductor)
    Differential exp.: edgeR + limma; FDR < 0.01; fold change > 1 vs naive
    Pathway viz.     : Pathview (R/Bioconductor; KEGG mmu04064)
    Overrepresentation: gProfiler (GO:BP and KEGG databases)
    TF enrichment    : ChEA3 (ENCODE ChIP-seq library)
  Data deposited: GEO GSE260996

  Synergy/antagonism classification:
    Formula  : DAB_memory = [AB - (B + dAB + dB)] / (B + dAB + dB)
               AB  = expression under sequential A+B stimulation
               B   = naive media-treated expression
               dAB = change from A-only (A followed by media)
               dB  = change from B-only
    Threshold: synergy if DAB_memory > 0.25; antagonism if DAB_memory < -0.25
  Key findings:
    polyI:C->TNFa: 572 synergistic / 394 antagonistic transcripts
    CpG->TNFa    : 214 synergistic / 366 antagonistic transcripts
    polyI:C->LPS : 800 synergistic / 478 antagonistic transcripts
    CpG->LPS     : 777 synergistic / 630 antagonistic transcripts
    Synergistic genes enriched for NF-kB and TNF signalling (priming) / immune response (all)
    Antagonistic genes enriched for cell adhesion, signal transduction, NF-kB (tolerance)

  QC gate (BB8/BB9):
    Pass (BB8): rnaSignal > 0 -> dispose(rnaLibrary)
    Fail (BB9): rnaSignal <= 0 -> drain(rnaLibrary)


DEEP LEARNING MODEL
-------------------
Architecture : Multilayer perceptron (MLP); TensorFlow framework (Abadi et al. 2016, arXiv)
Input        : 181 features per gene per condition
               133 chromatin features: peak accessibility (CPM) and binding motif counts for
               18 TFs across 3 most proximal ATAC peaks in proximal promoter
               (-1500 to +500 bp from TSS) and distal promoter (-3000 to -1500 / +500 to +3000
               bp from TSS); includes chromatin regulators without motifs (EZH2, HDAC, NELFE)
               48 NF-kB features: peak height, AUC, and activation time per stimulus condition
Output       : 4-class gene expression classification
               Class 1: downregulated (< 0.66x naive)
               Class 2: unchanged (0.87-1.5x naive)
               Class 3: upregulated (3-10x naive)
               Class 4: highly upregulated (>= 20x naive)
Layers       : 2-3 hidden layers; layer 1 = n_input nodes; subsequent = half/quarter prior
Regularisation: 10% dropout after each layer
Activation   : ReLU
Optimiser    : Adam
Validation   : 5-fold cross-validation; 8894 total samples (genes x conditions)
Accuracy     : Combined (chromatin + NF-kB): 72.8%
               Random baseline              : 38.7%
               NF-kB features only          : 61.8%
               Chromatin features only      : 64.7%
               Best 4-motif subset          : 51.2%
Top motifs   : RelA (present in all top-10 motif combinations) > Fos (AP-1) > Stat1/Stat2 >
               c/EBPD > Irf3 > Irf7 > Irf8
Code         : GitHub: taylab/macrophage_memory; DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.14337874

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Hemagglutination Assays for Blood Typing, Donor Compatibility Testing, and Hematocrit Analysis

REAGENTS USED:
  - Whole Blood
  - Reconstitution Solvent
  - Anti-A, Anti-B, Anti-AB, and Anti-D Blood Typing Antibodies (lyophilized)
  - Hematocrit Reagent (chemical agglutination agent)

STEPS:
1. Reconstitute lyophilized antibodies and hematocrit reagents using the reconstitution solvent and mix for 5s.
2. Meter whole-blood unit-droplets for each parallel test channel (A, B, AB, D, and hematocrit).
3. Merge each whole-blood droplet with its respective reconstituted reagent and mix for 10s to form the test droplet.

This protocol describes a label-free, shear-modulated inertial microfluidic system for the
enrichment and purification of ring-stage Plasmodium falciparum malaria parasites from lysed

of inertial lift forces in high-aspect-ratio microchannels: white blood cells (WBCs, 6-15 um)

diagnostics. Without enrichment, qPCR of whole blood at clinically relevant parasitemia
(~2k/mL) is technically impossible due to WBC DNA cross-reactivity and PCR inhibitors.
After microfluidic enrichment, detection reaches ~1 parasite/uL, approximately 100-fold
more sensitive than conventional microscopy of thick blood smears (50-100 parasites/uL).

--------
This protocol describes an automated digital-microfluidic (DMF) microbioreactor capable of
culturing and analyzing three distinct microorganism types -- bacteria, algae and yeast -- in

in a ~70 uL droplet ("mother drop") confined to a reactor region, kept in suspension by
automated semi-continuous circular-path mixing, and periodically sampled via daughter droplets

mother drop, preserving culture volume over multi-day growth curves. The platform was validated

on-chip processes: a fluorescent cell-viability assay and genetic transformation.

     reactor architecture, with organism-specific temperature and mixing regimes
  2. Absorbance-based density monitoring (600 nm bacteria/yeast, 660 nm algae) via
     daughter-droplet dispense onto transparent L-shaped electrode windows
  3. On-chip fluorescent viability assay of yeast using Ethidium homodimer-1 (EthD-1),
     with Triton X-100 as a lytic positive control
  4. On-chip genetic transformation of E. coli with a YFP reporter plasmid via
     CaCl2/heat-shock, followed by off-chip plating for colony confirmation

Growth rates measured on-chip were comparable to macroscale culture for all three organisms
(doubling times: E. coli 1.23 +/- 0.43 h vs. 0.79 +/- 0.06 h macroscale; S. cerevisiae
1.88 +/- 0.15 h vs. 1.80 +/- 0.24 h; C. cryptica 42.6 +/- 2.4 h vs. 37.0 +/- 1.2 h),

actuation, detector geometry).

Spacer       : 350 um, formed from five-high stacks of double-sided tape between plates.

Device regions:

    ~70 uL mother drop, actuated in a circular path (four adjacent-electrode movements,
    ~1.5 s actuation) for semi-continuous mixing.
  - Sample region: three rows of eleven 3 x 3 mm electrodes (one row per organism), used
    to drive daughter droplets to the absorbance-measurement electrodes.
  - Reservoir region: three 6 x 6 mm electrodes (one per sample row), used to dispense
    assay/transformation reagents for on-demand merging with sample droplets.

uncorrelated with NF-kB dynamics (Pearson r = -0.06), despite NF-kB being the
master transcription factor controlling TNF production. Computational modeling of the
LPS/TLR4 pathway identifies TRIF-mediated post-transcriptional regulation as the key
determinant of noisy and uncorrelated TNF secretion at the single-cell level.

Title        : Direct Detection and Drug-Resistance Profiling of Bacteremias Using Inertial Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://pubs.rsc.org/lc/article/15/10/2297/1246161/Direct-detection-and-drug-resistance-profiling-of
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1039/c5lc00311c

Platform     : Inertial microfluidics (Dean Flow Fractionation) + NanoString hybridization-based RNA detection


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a method for rapid isolation of bacteria from whole blood using a PDMS
spiral microchannel device operating on the principle of Dean Flow Fractionation (DFF), coupled
to hybridization-based RNA detection (NanoString nCounter) for direct pathogen identification
and antibiotic susceptibility determination without bacterial culture or enzymatic amplification.

The protocol encodes two sequential diagnostic workflows:

  Workflow 1 | Species identification via rRNA detection:
    Bacteria (~100 cfu/mL) isolated from 3x-diluted whole blood by DFF; rRNA probes targeting
    species-variable regions of 16S and 23S rRNA identify E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and
    P. aeruginosa from concentrated bacterial eluate. Sensitivity approaches clinically relevant
    uncultured bacteremia loads without PCR or enzymatic amplification.

  Workflow 2 | Antibiotic susceptibility via mRNA detection:
    E. coli clinical isolates at ~10^5 cfu/mL (direct spike or 7.5 h BACTEC pre-enrichment
    from 1 cfu/mL) processed by DFF; recovered bacteria exposed to ciprofloxacin (2.5 mcg/mL,
    37 C, 30 min); mRNA transcriptional response profiled by NanoString. Transcriptional
    Susceptibility Score discriminates susceptible (score ~0) from resistant (score ~1) strains.

Total workflow time: ~8 hours including DFF separation, RNA hybridization, and ciprofloxacin
exposure. This represents a >6-fold acceleration over standard culture-based methods (48-72 h).


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material  : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) cast from silanized silicon wafer master; bonded
            irreversibly to glass slide by air plasma (Harrick Plasma Cleaner).
Channel   : Spiral geometry; 500 um (w) x 80 um (h); total length ~10 cm.
            Height fixed at 80 um so that blood cells (ap/h > 0.07) experience inertial
            lift (F_L) while bacteria (<1 um, ap/h << 0.07) are governed by Dean drag (F_D) only.

Inlets:
  Outer inlet (75 um wide)  : 3x diluted whole blood sample (~15% hematocrit)
  Inner inlet (425 um wide) : PBS + 0.1% BSA sheath fluid at ~10x sample flow rate

Outlets:
  Bacterial outlet (200 um) : Bacteria and platelets (Dean-migrated to outer wall, DC1 complete)
  Waste outlet              : RBCs and leukocytes (inertially focused at inner wall)

Separation principle:
  Dean drag (F_D) migrates all particles toward the inner wall. RBCs (~6-8 um) and leukocytes
  (~7-12 um) satisfy ap/h > 0.07 and are arrested at the inner wall by inertial lift forces (F_L).
  Bacteria (<1 um) and platelets (~2-3 um) are unaffected by F_L; they complete one full Dean
  Cycle (DC1), recirculating from inner to outer wall, and exit at the bacterial outlet.
  Separation is label-free, species-independent, and based solely on physical size.

  Syringe pumps : PHD 2000 (Harvard Apparatus) x2 (separate pumps for sample and sheath)

  High-speed camera : Phantom v9 (Vision Research) for blood cell imaging
  Flow cytometer : BD Accuri C6 (BD Biosciences) for separation efficiency quantification
  Centrifuge    : 16,000 x g for bacterial eluate pelleting

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a label-free, size-based method for isolating viable circulating tumor cells
(CTCs) from peripheral blood using a spiral inertial microfluidic biochip. CTCs -- rare cancer cells
shed from primary or metastatic tumors into the bloodstream -- occur at frequencies as low as one cell
per 10^7-10^9 hematological cells in metastatic cancer patients, making reliable isolation a major
technical challenge.

The spiral biochip exploits the combined effect of inertial lift force (FL) and Dean drag force (FD)
in a curvilinear microchannel. Larger CTCs (typically 15-20 um) focus near the inner wall at the
outlet, while smaller blood cells (RBCs 3-8 um, WBCs 10-15 um, platelets 3-8 um) migrate along
Dean vortex streamlines toward the outer wall. This passive, continuous-flow separation requires no
antibodies, magnetic beads, or external force fields.

Key performance metrics:
  - >=85% CTC recovery across multiple cancer cell lines
  - 99.99% WBC depletion (4-log) from healthy samples
  - 7.5 mL lysed blood processed in 37.5 min (single chip) or 12.5 min (3x multiplexed chip)
  - CTCs collected in suspension (viable), compatible with culture, FISH, and sequencing

The protocol has been validated in clinical samples from patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung
cancer (n=15; 10-1535 CK+ CTCs isolated) and breast cancer (n=15; 12-1275 CK+ CTCs isolated),
with a negative-control threshold of >7 CK+ cells per sample defining a positive patient.


SEPARATION PHYSICS
------------------
The spiral microchannel has a rectangular cross-section (500 um wide x 170 um deep) in a two-loop
configuration with radius of curvature ~10 mm. Flow in the curved channel generates secondary
cross-sectional Dean vortices perpendicular to the primary flow direction. The Dean number is:

    De = Re * sqrt(DH / 2*RC)

where Re is the Reynolds number, DH is the hydraulic diameter, and RC is the radius of curvature.
The Dean migration velocity is:

    U_Dean = 1.8e-4 * De^1.63

For particles with diameter comparable to channel dimensions (ac/h > 0.07), inertial lift forces
(shear-induced FL_shear and wall-induced FL_wall) direct cells to equilibrium focusing positions.
The balance of FL and FD results in two focusing positions near the inner channel wall for larger
CTCs, while smaller cells disperse and follow Dean streamlines toward the outer wall.

Design parameters: 75 um sample inlet (outer) / 425 um sheath inlet (inner); 150 um CTC collection
outlet (inner) / 350 um waste outlet (outer). Size cutoff: ~12 um (CTCs >=12 um recoverable).

Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-019-0435-1
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-019-0435-1

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a PCR-free integrated microfluidic platform for absolute quantification
of free-floating and extracellular vesicle (EV)-contained microRNAs (miRNAs) directly from
untreated human plasma or serum. The platform integrates two chips in series:

  Chip 1 (SAW lysing chip): Surface acoustic waves (SAWs) generated by interdigitated electrodes
    on a LiNbO3 piezoelectric substrate mechanically lyse EVs under continuous flow, releasing
    their miRNA cargo without chemical reagents.

  Chip 2 (Concentration/sensing chip): Two sets of ion-exchange membranes (IEMs) — a cation-
    exchange membrane (CEM) for electrokinetic concentration and an anion-exchange membrane (AEM)
    functionalized with a target-specific oligoprobe as the sensor — detect and quantify the target
    miRNA via current-voltage curve (CVC) shift in the over-limiting current region.

The two chips are connected by a 500 um diameter, 10 cm Tygon tube enabling uninterrupted sample
transfer with no analyte loss between stages. By conducting two sequential 30-minute measurements
— one with the SAW device OFF (free-floating miRNA only) and one with it ON (total miRNA: free-
floating + EV-released) — the EV-miRNA fraction is directly computed from the difference in
voltage shift (Delta-V) between the two runs.

Target biomarker: miRNA hsa-mir-21-5p (miR-21; sequence: TAGCTTATCAGACTGATGTTGA), associated
with pancreatic, lung, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma.

Key advantages over conventional RT-qPCR:
  - No EV extraction, RNA purification, reverse transcription, or amplification required
  - Assay time: 30 min per measurement (vs. 13 h for RT-qPCR)
  - Sample volume: 20 uL per measurement (vs. 1 mL for RT-qPCR)
  - Quantification uncertainty: <10% (absolute quantification)
  - Detection limit: 1 pM

-------------------
Chip 1 — SAW Lysing Chip
  Substrate  : 128 deg YX lithium niobate (LiNbO3), piezoelectric
  Electrodes : 20 pairs of interdigitated aluminum electrodes (200 nm thick; 20 nm Ti adhesion)
               Width-controlled single-phase unidirectional IDT; resonant frequency: 28 MHz
  Channel    : Polycarbonate, 15 x 2 x 0.3 mm (l/w/t); attached with double-sided Kapton tape
               Channel oriented parallel to IDTs; SAW propagates perpendicular to channel
  Operation  : SAW generated at 28 MHz, 1 W (Agilent 33250A + E&I 325LA RF amplifier)
               Acoustic pressure shears EV membranes; ~1 min exposure at 250 uL/h achieves
               ~100% EV lysis (50% more efficient than TRIzol chemical lysis)

Chip 2 — Concentration/Sensing Chip
  Material   : Polycarbonate (three-layer), 60 x 2 x 0.3 mm (l/w/t)

PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | Master Mix Preparation
  For each of the five reactions, independently combine in a 5 mL Eppendorf tube:
    ddPCR Supermix + Nuclease-Free H2O + Primer Y87 + Primer Y88 + FAM Probe
  Mix each build sequentially (mix for 5 s per addition, 4 additions = 20 s total).
  Vortex briefly; spin down before use. Keep on ice until needed.

Step 2 | Serial Dilution (7 steps, 96-well non-skirted PCR plate)
  Use fresh siliconised tubes or low-binding PCR plate. Change tips between every step.

  Dilution 1 (D1): Add 39 uL nuclease-free H2O to row 1. Add 1 uL of AAV sample.
                   Mix 20 uL by pipetting up and down 20 times. Dilution = 1:40 (2.5e-2).
  Dilution 2 (D2): Transfer 10 uL from D1 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-3).
  Dilution 3 (D3): Transfer 10 uL from D2 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-4).
  Dilution 4 (D4): Transfer 10 uL from D3 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-5).
  Dilution 5 (D5): Transfer 10 uL from D4 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-6).
  Dilution 6 (D6): Transfer 10 uL from D5 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-7).
  Dilution 7 (D7): Transfer 10 uL from D6 into 90 uL H2O. Mix 10x. Factor 1:10 (2.5e-8).

  Seal plate with Microseal B. Store at 4 C until reaction assembly.
  Reactions are loaded with D4, D5, D6, D7 (linear detection range: 100-10,000 copies/uL).

Step 3 | PCR Reaction Assembly
  Using multichannel pipette, dispense 31.5 uL master mix into each 8-strip PCR tube.
  Add 1.5 uL of the appropriate dilution (D4, D5, D6, D7) to each tube.
  For the positive control tube: add 1.5 uL of iDreV DNA at 2.5e-6 dilution.
  Vortex and spin down each tube twice before loading to DG8 cartridge.
  Bench temperature vortex/spin step modelled as heat at 20 C for 10 s in BioScript.

Step 4 | Droplet Generation (Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Generator)
  Pour Droplet Generation Oil (Bio-Rad 1863005) into the oil reservoir.
  Load 22.2 uL of each sample reaction into the middle row of a DG8 cartridge.
    IMPORTANT: Pipette slowly. Avoid introducing bubbles. Use reverse-pipetting technique.
  Load 70 uL Droplet Generation Oil slowly into the bottom row of each DG8 well.
  Cover cartridge with the DG8 Gasket (Bio-Rad 1863009).
  Insert cartridge into QX200 Droplet Generator. Run droplet generation.
  Target: approximately 20,000 droplets per well (~0.85 nL each).
  Using a multichannel pipette set to 40 uL, transfer droplets from the top well of
  the DG8 cartridge to the appropriate well of the ddPCR 96-Well Plate (Bio-Rad 12001925).
    IMPORTANT: Pipette very slowly (1 uL/s). Do not tilt or agitate the plate after transfer.
  Seal plate with Pierceable Foil Heat Seal (Bio-Rad 1814040) using the PX1 Plate Sealer
  at 95 C for 5 s.

Step 5 | PCR Thermocycling
  Run the sealed ddPCR plate on a Bio-Rad C1000 Touch Thermocycler (or equivalent).
  Ramp rate: 2 C/s. Lid temperature: 105 C.

  Programme:
    Stage 1: 95 C  for 10 min  (600 s)   -- Hot-start enzyme activation
    Stage 2: 94 C  for 30 s  \
    Stage 3: 60 C  for 60 s   > 40 cycles -- Amplification
    Stage 4: 98 C  for 10 min  (600 s)   -- Droplet signal stabilisation
    Stage 5:  4 C  hold                   -- Until droplet reader transfer

  BioScript IR representation (no loop construct; cycles unrolled as accumulated duration):
    heat at 95 C for 600 s   (stage 1)
    heat at 94 C for 1200 s  (stage 2: 40 x 30 s)
    heat at 60 C for 2400 s  (stage 3: 40 x 60 s)
    heat at 98 C for 600 s   (stage 4)
    heat at  4 C for 60 s    (stage 5 hold abstraction)

Step 6 | Droplet Reader Run (QC Gate 1: Reader Validity)
  Open QuantaSoft software. Load template: ITR-Shenqin-24 (24-sample configuration).
  Per-well template settings:
    Sample name: [sample ID]  |  ABS  |  ddPCR mMix no dUTP  |  FAM  |  Ch1 Unknown
  Load Droplet Reader Oil (Bio-Rad 1863004) into the reader reservoir. Prime reader.
  Place ddPCR plate in reader with black clasps facing down.
  Run experiment in FAM/VIC mode, reading by row.
  Set amplitude threshold to 1000 in QuantaSoft.

  QC Gate (BB2/BB3) -- keyed on D4 (highest expected signal):
    PASS (readerSignal4 > 0): >10,000 droplets per well; clear FAM+/FAM- separation.
                              Proceed to positive control QC.
    FAIL (readerSignal4 <= 0): Insufficient droplets or no FAM signal detected.
                               Repeat droplet generation from Step 4.

Step 7 | Positive Control QC Gate (QC Gate 2: Assay Validation)
  Apply dropletReaderDetection to the positive control well (iDreV at 2.5e-6 dilution).
  Expected result: 300-700 copies/uL.

  QC Gate (BB5/BB6):
    PASS (controlSignal > 0): iDreV within 300-700 copies/uL range.
                              Master mix composition and cycling validated.
                              Proceed to titer calculation.
    FAIL (controlSignal <= 0): iDreV out of expected range.
                               Investigate master mix assembly and cycling programme.
                               Do not report sample titers until positive control passes.

Step 8 | Titer Calculation (off-chip, QuantaSoft)
  In QuantaSoft, identify dilutions D4-D7 within the linear detection range
  (100-10,000 copies/uL). Dilutions outside this range (oversaturated or under-detected)
  are excluded.
  Average the concentrations from dilutions within the linear range.
  Back-calculate viral titer:
    Genome copies/mL = (avg copies/uL) x 1000 / (dilution_factor x (1.5 uL / 33 uL))
  Report titer as vg/mL.

Step 9 | Cleanup
  Discard used DG8 cartridges and gaskets as biohazard waste.
  Wipe down hood and bench surfaces with 70% ethanol.
  Dispose of AAV-containing materials per institutional biosafety guidelines.

SSA strategy:
  lilott8/BioScript enforces strict single-assignment. Every variable may be consumed
  (appear as argument to mix/detect/heat/dispose) exactly once. The split keyword
  (syntax: result = split source into N) was avoided because: (a) all N output elements
  must be consumed or the compiler flags stranded droplets, and (b) correct syntax
  requires an integer literal (result = split source into N) which was missing in
  earlier versions causing ValueError in visitSplit. Instead, each manifest is used as
  a reservoir tapped by independent dispense calls; each tap produces a unique SSA token
  consumed exactly once downstream.

drain keyword:
  lilott8/BioScript has no visitDrain method (confirmed from ir_visitor.py). The drain
  keyword in .bs source compiles to dispose() in IR. Both pass and fail branch arms
  emit dispose() in the IR; only one arm executes at runtime (exclusive branches).

heat() in IR:
  heat() is an in-place mutation. The same variable token appears in multiple heat()
  calls (e.g. droplets4 through all 5 PCR stages) then is consumed once by a subsequent
  mix() or detect(). This is correct BioScript IR semantics, not an SSA violation.
  The IR counter showing N>2 appearances for heat-processed variables is expected.

  UnicodeDecodeError at compile time. All such characters have been replaced with ASCII
  equivalents (hyphen, C, u, ->, x).
